the liver phospholipids are the key regulators of the triglyceride metabolism in the liver, and that the liver phosphatidic acids are the key regulators in the liver phospholipoproteins formation and secretion.

liver PL is a limiting factor for liver lipoproteins and that the liver is an important site of phospholipide metabolism.

the role of liver phosphatides and their exchange in plasma in the transport of lipid from the liver to other sites of utilization.
the interrelationship of liver phospholipo lipase, phospholipid, and triglyceride metabolism.
the interrelationships between liver phospholipids and liver lipid transport, and between the liver and adipose tissue in the triglycerides cycle.

liver PL synthesis, transport and turnover are closely interrelated to liver TG metabolism and that the liver PL is a key factor in the regulation of liver TG transport.

liver PL turnover and synthesis are related to the mobilization of liver TG for extrahepatic utilization and for storage in the adipose tissue for recycling via the TG cycle.

the liver plays a major role in the regulation of plasma phospholipoproteins.
